data.title: RBI alert about AI-driven cyber risks, banks taking steps to plug vulnerabilities: Sanjay Malhotra
data.description:
RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra on Friday said the central bank and other banks are alert about emerging cyber risks posed by artificial intelligence (AI) agents and are taking measures to identify and plug vulnerabilities in their IT systems.

Referring to reports of AI agents operating in test mode that allegedly attacked banks overseas and stole data, Malhotra said such risks were real but could be addressed by keeping banking systems secure.

There are reports that major US banks have detected third-party AI agents inside customer accounts, raising concerns that automated tools could act beyond instructions given by customers.

"Our banks, the government as well as the RBI, we have alerted them, and they are conscious about it and they are taking measures to ensure that such kind of vulnerabilities, wherever they are, are plugged," he said at the NDTV World Summit.

The statement comes in the backdrop of the State Bank of India (SBI) acknowledging suspected exposure of 3,897 customer records with personally identifiable information on the dark web.

The RBI Governor said the central bank has a strong team, appropriate regulations and supervisory mechanisms, along with experts who audit the IT systems of major banks and non-banking financial companies (NBFCs).

The RBI is in continuous dialogue with banks and NBFCs to strengthen their IT infrastructure and ensure compliance with the prescribed regulations, he said.

Malhotra said the focus is on two key areas — data security and protection against cyberattacks – that could disrupt banking systems and cause downtime.

While the RBI has a robust regulatory and supervisory framework, the rapid pace of software development means that vulnerabilities can sometimes emerge, he said.

"It is our endeavour that we identify these vulnerabilities as soon as possible and plug them through the patches that have to be deployed in these IT systems,” he added.

On the FCNR deposit repayment, Malhotra said, the RBI has sufficient reserves and time to pay back the foreign currency non-resident (bank) deposits it garnered under its special concessional window.

“I am very optimistic that our external sector is very resilient, very strong. We already have sufficient money and reserves to pay that, but we will have even more than that. And the average deposit size is four years plus, so we have sufficient time to repay,” he said.

On June 8, the RBI unveiled a facility under which it would bear the full hedging costs for banks raising fresh 3-5 year FCNR(B) deposits, which closed on August 31, a month ahead of the original deadline.

The RBI received USD 132.98 billion worth of FCNR(B) deposits under the scheme.

Malhotra expressed confidence that India's external sector is very strong in the medium-term.

"I am optimistic that in the medium term the balance of payments and the external situation is going to be strong," he said.

"We already have sufficient forex reserves by all metrics. We built on them, we reinforced them, through the FCNR(B) scheme as you are aware. All other parameters, like services exports, remittances, among others, also point to a strong external sector in the medium-term,” he added.

data.title: Fast-fashion group Shein agrees to pay $100 million to settle US FTC probe
data.description:
Key points:
  • Settlement equals nearly half of second-quarter profit
  • FTC has received 12,000 complaints about Shein since 2020
  • Regulatory headwinds in EU, US have slowed e-commerce growth

By Helen Reid and Jody Godoy

Chinese fast-fashion giant Shein has agreed to pay $100 million to settle an investigation by the US Federal Trade Commission over delivery delays and other customer complaints, a source with direct knowledge told Reuters on Friday.

The settlement, equivalent to 44% of Shein's second-quarter profit, is the latest to hit the online fast-fashion retailer facing a regulatory and tax crackdown in Europe and the US that has slammed the brakes on its growth.

Shein, founded in China though headquartered in Singapore, said in a statement to Reuters that it had "reached a constructive outcome with the FTC", and that additional information would be shared soon. An FTC spokesperson declined to comment.

The company had warned in July filings for its Hong Kong IPO that the US probe could lead to significant fines.

Consumers filed more than 12,000 complaints about Shein over more than $11 million in purchases between January 2020 and June 2026, according to FTC records reviewed by Reuters.

At least some of those relate to shipping, with customers reporting to the FTC and Better Business Bureau that they never received packages that Shein had marked as delivered, and that Shein customer service did not resolve the issue.

Reuters was not able to independently verify the substance of the complaints, or whether they were ultimately resolved.

As well as selling its own-brand clothing, Shein's website also operates as a marketplace where third-party sellers offer everything from toys to household appliances and decor.

MORE PAIN AHEAD FOR SHEIN WITH HIGHER EU FEES

Shein shares have already dropped 22% from their September 1 listing price as investors realised the extent to which the European Union's €3 fees on low-value e-commerce packages have bruised its business there.

And there's further pain ahead for Shein, with the EU imposing an additional €2 handling fee from November 1, making the total fee €5 per separate customs code.

"The way these tariffs are implemented is extra punishing for Shein," said Mike Ryan, head of e-commerce insights at Smarter Ecommerce, who has tracked how Shein has dialled down its spending on Google Ads visibility in Europe.

Shein was known for selling $5 dresses and $10 jeans, but has been forced to raise its prices as the US and then Europe closed customs duty loopholes.

CEO Sky Xu said last month that Shein would develop more higher-priced brands in an attempt to boost profitability.

Shein is also still under investigation by the European Commission over illegal products on its marketplace. It was fined €150 million ($168 million) by France's data protection authority over the improper use of cookies last year.

It's not the first time the US FTC has taken action against online retailers over deliveries.

US firm Fashion Nova was fined $9.3 million in 2020 for failing to meet shipping promises to customers and giving them gift cards instead of refunds.

Crocs Inc-owned Hey Dude was also fined $1.95 million in 2023 for failing to notify customers of shipping delays and suppressing negative reviews.

data.title: The Week in Oil: Fears of U.S.-Iran Escalation Push Brent to $117
data.description:
By Giulia Petroni

Here is a look at what happened in oil markets in the week of Oct. 19-23 and what the focus will be in the days to come.

OVERVIEW: Oil prices are on track for another weekly gain on fears of renewed escalation between the U.S. and Iran after the midterm elections. Brent crude, the global oil benchmark, was around $117 a barrel in midmorning U.S. trade, while West Texas Intermediate was just below $103 a barrel.

MACRO: Rising energy costs are fueling concerns over inflation and interest-rate hikes. According to the FedWatch tool, traders broadly expect the U.S. central bank to leave interest rates unchanged next week, but they see a nearly 80% probability of a hike in December.

Meanwhile, consumer sentiment in the U.S. ticked lower in October, hovering near record-low levels, according to the University of Michigan's survey. Inflation expectations instead moved slightly higher.

GEOPOLITICAL RISKS: Fears that the U.S. could attack Iran after the midterm elections in early November are driving oil's rise this week. The U.S. has a third aircraft carrier strike group and an additional Marine expeditionary unit en route to the Middle East, while the military has moved some troops off bases in the region.

The buildup comes at a politically sensitive moment, with Israel's general election scheduled for Oct. 27 and the U.S. midterms a week later.

Tehran warned that a renewed U.S. and Israeli air campaign would prompt retaliation extending well beyond military targets. Iran threatened strikes on American bases and warships, as well as airports, pipelines and other civilian infrastructure in neighboring Persian Gulf countries.

At the same time, persistent attacks on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz and deadly strikes by Yemen's Houthi militants on Saudi Arabia are keeping the geopolitical risk premium high. The market's focus is less on how much oil is available today than on whether Middle East exports can be sustained if fighting intensifies again.

SUPPLY AND DEMAND: Kpler data show that oil flows through the Strait of Hormuz remain 26% below prewar levels, with the seven-day average at 12.65 million barrels a day, compared with a baseline of 17.15 million. Continued attacks on shipping are sustaining a risk premium in both freight rates and crude prices. Yet total Middle Eastern oil supplies reaching global markets, excluding Iran, remain above prewar levels.

Meanwhile, shipment of Russian diesel could be headed for the U.S., according to vessel-tracking data, potentially signaling a return of direct fuel deliveries as U.S. President Trump seeks to expand Russian supplies to international markets.

WHAT'S AHEAD: Markets will turn to the Federal Reserve's policy meeting on Oct. 27-28 and the release of the Fed's preferred inflation gauge, the personal consumption expenditures price index, on Oct. 29 for clues on the outlook for interest rates. On the energy front, next week's focus will be on any signs of a potential escalation between the U.S. and Iran, fresh data on crude and refined-product inventories, and developments in Russian diesel shipments.

data.title: Government asks industry bodies to tighten certification checks, conduct regular cybersecurity audits
data.description:
New Delhi, October 23: The Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) has asked sectoral associations and industry bodies to strengthen certification processes and conduct regular security audits to prevent a recurrence of cybersecurity incidents such as the recent PHP vulnerabilities and security lapses involving eMudhra, a senior government official said.

“We have written to all the concerned industry bodies and associations to get better updates on certifications and regular audits to avoid such security incidents in future,” MeitY Secretary S Krishnan told businessline on the sidelines of an event here.

The government is reviewing a series of cybersecurity incidents reported over the past two days. The PHP Foundation, which maintains the programming language used by millions of websites, announced an urgent security update to address two critical vulnerabilities. Separately, Indian digital trust services provider eMudhra was found to have used weak security keys to issue website certificates.

Data Exposure

The country’s largest lender, State Bank of India (SBI), also disclosed an incident involving the suspected exposure of customer data on the dark web.

Krishnan said the government was monitoring the developments and assessing what steps could be taken to help affected sectors address such incidents.

On cybersecurity, the Secretary said that it was crucial to remind ourselves again that securing data infrastructure was critically important.

While on one hand India was expanding the capacity of digital transactions and digital way of doing business across the range of industries as it was a matter of convenience, “it has many other spin-offs” too, Krishnan said.

Work to be Done

“There’s a whole range of digital public infrastructure which needs to be built for various sectors. In each of these areas, there’s work to be done and it needs to be expanded to a number of other places where, we can transact digitally. But, equally, very important at this point in time is to make sure that we are able to do this in a secure way,” he said.

Krishnan said the world is dealing with a number of cybersecurity episodes over the last two/ three days — some of them linked to AI — and some of them linked to other elements.

“I think it’s very important to remind ourselves again that securing a lot of this infrastructure and securing the way that these services are delivered is critically important,” Krishnan mentioned in a fireside chat round at KPMG’s Agrasar Bharat Manch 2026 event here.

Bigger Risks

He said it was interesting to note that many of the ways in which rogue agents are able to exploit and enter into systems is because somebody has not followed elementary cyber hygiene and therefore that becomes, again, an element of how organisations go about looking at these issues.

“I think these two aspects really need to work. On the one hand, expanding the capacity of digital transactions and digital way of doing business across a range of other issues. The second part of it is building an AI layer over it, so that with all the data which we have, we get better insights, better ways in which this can be used, easier ways in which it works,” Krishnan said.

And at the same time, make sure that all the cybersecurity related aspects of this, are addressed effectively because we shouldn’t open ourselves to bigger risks, he added.

data.title: JK Tyre Q2 net profit declines by 71% y-o-y to ₹65 crore due to geopolitical tensions
data.description:
Hit by operating environment and geopolitical tensions in West Asia, JK Tyre & Industries (JK Tyre) on Friday reported a y-o-y decline of 71.30 per cent in its consolidated net profit to₹65.11 crore in the second quarter this year as compared with ₹227 crore in the same period last year.

EBITDA margin contracted sharply to 7.1 per cent from 13.3 per cent.

However, consolidated revenue from operations grew by around 21 per cent y-o-y to around ₹4,841 crore during the quarter in review as compared with around ₹4,011 crore in the corresponding period last financial year (FY25).

Speaking to reporters, Anshuman Singhania, Managing Director, JK Tyre said that the operating environment remains challenging due to geopolitical tensions in West Asia and the input costs were “persistently higher”, and there were supply chain constraints, including container freight rates that are significantly above historical levels.

He said that the cost of raw materials increased around 9 per cent in the Q2 from the Q1 this year and the cumulative increase over the first six months of the financial year has been around 30 per cent.

And, therefore, “Going further to the third quarter, we are seeing another 4-5 per cent increase in the full raw material basket,” he said adding that the impact will be passed on to the customers.

“We intend to increase prices in the third quarter in the range of 4-5 per cent,” Singhania said. JK Tyre had increased the prices by 5 per cent in Q1, followed by another 7 per cent in the Q2.

Growth momentum

Meanwhile, talking about India business, Raghupati Singhania, Chairman and Managing Director, JK Tyre, said, “India business has picked up significant growth momentum post GST 2.0, anchoring an increase in original equipment (OE) market by 65 per cent, leading to 32 per cent growth in domestic sales, on a y-o-y basis. This has been delivered through disciplined execution across markets and segments.”

He further added that the company remains optimistic on the demand backed by healthy customer traction visible across segments in the coming quarters.

Shares of JK Tyre closed at ₹309.20 apiece on the BSE on Friday, down by 4.30 per cent from the previous close.

data.title: Western Digital Stock Falls Despite Visibility to 2031
data.description:
Western Digital reported fiscal first-quarter non-GAAP EPS of $4.64, above the analysts' consensus of $4.11, on revenue of $4.38 billion, up 55% from a year earlier and ahead of the $4.14 billion estimate. Western Digital shares fell 2.87% in premarket.

Non-GAAP gross margin widened to 58.1% from 43.9% a year earlier, and non-GAAP operating margin reached 49.1%. CFO Kris Sennesael credited robust exabyte growth and improved pricing. Free cash flow was $1.38 billion, and the company repurchased $1.0 billion of stock in the quarter. It also raised its quarterly dividend 17% to $0.175 per share.

For the fiscal second quarter, Western Digital guided revenue to $5.1 billion, plus or minus $100 million, or growth of 66% to 72% year over year, with non-GAAP gross margin of 60% to 61% and non-GAAP EPS of $5.80, plus or minus $0.20. On the earnings call, CEO Irving Tan said Western Digital has good visibility up to 2030, 2031 across its top seven customers, and that their demand signal keeps rising quarter after quarter.
